designs.title: Byron Bay
designs.why: Clean binary art (no partial alpha, no specks), strong arched title and the lighthouse reads as Byron at 3 m. The left pandanus thicket is a near-solid mass, so white ink on black gets heavy there, and the wave face holds hundreds of 0.3-0.4 mm reverse slits that will plug with ink spread on a dark tee.
designs.fix: Open up the left foliage mass and widen the reverse slits in the wave face to at least 0.5 mm (6 px) so the white-ink print on black keeps its engraving instead of going solid.

designs.title: Playa Venao
designs.why: Good balance: palm, signpost and an open bay give clear figure-ground, and the sign lettering (SURF/EXPLORE/RELAX/REPEAT) holds at full size. Same production risk as the set: very fine reverse water and wave lines under 0.4 mm that fill in on black, and a thin dashed inner ring that is close to the minimum line for a 156-230 mesh.
designs.fix: Thicken the dashed inner ring to about 0.5 mm and open the tightest reverse lines in the wave and surf foam.

designs.title: Ericeira
designs.why: Most specific scene in the set (whitewashed clifftop town, stone steps, longboard), so it doesn't read as a generic beach. Big area of open sky, so ink coverage is lighter and the black-ink-on-white main tee will print crisp. The building windows and stonework are dense, but still above the plug-in threshold for black on white.
designs.fix: Thin out the hatching on the cliff face under the town so that on the black tee (white ink) the cliff doesn't merge into one solid block.

designs.title: San Juan del Sur
designs.why: Prints cleanly and the Christ statue on the headland is a nice local touch, but the longest name forces a tight arc with small letters, so the title is the weakest read at 3 m. The bottom-left sign cluster plus the palm plus the dense hill make a busy, dark corner.
designs.fix: Set the title a size larger by tightening the tracking and pulling the arc a little lower, and simplify the sign cluster to three boards.

designs.title: Haleiwa
designs.why: The art is fine (Ka'ena-style ridge, wave, SHAVE ICE sign, good local cues), but the title tracking is so wide that HALEIWA reads as loose separate letters next to its tighter-set siblings, and the H/A sit close to the ring. Fine reverse slits in the wave will close on the black main tee.
designs.fix: Tighten the title tracking by about 30% and centre it on the arc so it reads as one word. Open the wave-face slits to 0.5 mm or more for the white-on-black run.

designs.title: Puerto Escondido
designs.why: The barrel wave is the hero and it's big and correct for Zicatela. The palapa and headland frame it well and the sky stays open, so coverage is moderate. The long title fits the arc with good clearance from the ring. The dark tube interior is made of 0.3-0.4 mm reverse slits that ink gain will fill, so on the black tee it turns into a white blob.
designs.fix: Rework the tube interior with fewer, wider reverse slits (6-8 px) so the barrel keeps its form through ink spread on both tees.

designs.title: Montañita
designs.why: Best storytelling in the set: the beach bar with the SURF/FOOD/MUSIC/FRIENDS sign, string lights and steps gives it a real vibe, and the Ñ tilde is drawn cleanly. Heavy black mass under the thatch roof is the main ink-load spot, but overall coverage is about 30%, which is OK for a soft plastisol hand.
designs.fix: Break up the solid shadow under the thatch with a few wider reverse lines so it doesn't print as a stiff, solid white patch on the black main tee.

designs.title: Tamarindo
designs.why: Simplest, calmest scene with the most negative space, so it's the easiest separation to hold and the lightest hand on a $50 tee. The sun breaking the ring on the right is a nice badge move. It's a little generic (palm, wave, headland) with fewer local cues than the others, and the wave slits share the set's plug-in risk.
designs.fix: Add one Tamarindo-specific cue (for example the estuary mouth or a surfboard rack) in the empty lower-right beach, and open the wave slits to 0.5 mm or more.
